title: Observability
subtitle: Find failures through health, logs, metrics, and traces.
description: Expose selected Actuator endpoints, inspect application signals, and trace requests across services. Configure liveness, readiness, and startup probes.

lessons.title: Health & operational endpoints
lessons.summary: Actuator reports application and component health. Expose only the endpoints needed and protect sensitive information.
keyPoints: Expose selected endpoints rather than a wildcard.
A failing datasource indicator can make aggregate health DOWN.
Avoid exposing configuration, heap dumps, and other sensitive endpoints publicly.
practice: Expose health and info and restrict detailed health information.
Public health responses omit sensitive internals.

exercises.prompt: Expose only health and info through Actuator web endpoints, and show health details only to authorized users.
exercises.explanation: Endpoints such as env and heapdump can expose secrets or memory contents. Keep exposure narrow and access controlled.

exercises.prompt: The database is down and the datasource health indicator is active. What does aggregate health report by default?
options: DOWN with HTTP 503.
UP because the process is running.
HTTP 404.
The application automatically restarts.
exercises.explanation: DOWN maps to 503 so monitoring and load balancers can distinguish unavailable components.

lessons.title: Logs, metrics & traces
lessons.summary: Metrics summarize behavior, logs explain individual events, and traces connect operations within a request.
objectives: Choose a signal for an alert.
Keep sensitive data out of logs.
keyPoints: Metrics support rates, latency distributions, and alerts.
Trace IDs connect spans and related log entries.
Avoid passwords, tokens, personal data, and high-cardinality metric tags.
practice: Count created orders and log their internal IDs without full request headers.
Prometheus can query the counter and logs contain no credentials.

exercises.prompt: You need an alert when more than 5% of POST /orders requests fail over five minutes. Which signal fits best?
options: Metrics with status-tagged counters or timers
Manually reading every log every five minutes
One trace from the latest request
A heap dump
exercises.explanation: HTTP request metrics can be aggregated into error rates over a time window.

exercises.prompt: Create a Micrometer orders.created counter that increments whenever an order is created. Receive MeterRegistry through the constructor.
exercises.explanation: Prometheus exposes this counter as orders_created_total. Avoid tags such as individual order IDs.

exercises.prompt: Which log entry avoids sensitive request or customer data?
options: Log Order created with orderId and item count.
Log every request header including Authorization.
Log the login password at DEBUG.
Log a complete customer object containing identity numbers and addresses.
exercises.explanation: Log identifiers and technical context. Headers and full objects can contain secrets and personal information.

lessons.title: Tracing across services
lessons.summary: Distributed tracing joins spans across services so you can locate slow or failed operations.
objectives: Preserve trace context in HTTP clients.
keyPoints: Use auto-configured client builders to retain instrumentation.
traceparent carries IDs needed to join spans.
Sample deliberately; recording every production request has a cost.
practice: Connect Order and Inventory tracing and inspect one request across both services.
Both operations appear under the same trace ID.

exercises.prompt: Order and Inventory appear as separate traces. What is a likely cause?
options: Order uses RestClient.create(), bypassing the instrumented Boot builder.
Inventory uses a different port.
The services use different databases.
Sampling is set to 100%.
exercises.explanation: Boot’s auto-configured builder includes observation instrumentation. A manually created client can omit context propagation.

exercises.prompt: Which W3C Trace Context header carries trace and span IDs between services?
exercises.explanation: traceparent carries the trace ID, parent span ID, version, and flags.

exercises.prompt: Set tracing sampling to 100% for a development environment.
exercises.explanation: Full sampling is useful during development. Choose an appropriate production policy or collector-side tail sampling.

lessons.title: Liveness, readiness & startup
lessons.summary: Probes tell the platform when to send traffic and when a container needs restarting.
objectives: Keep shared dependencies out of liveness.
Configure separate readiness and liveness endpoints.
keyPoints: Readiness removes unready pods from service traffic.
Startup probes allow slow JVM startup before regular probes begin.
practice: Configure startup, readiness, and liveness probes for the application.
A database outage does not trigger unnecessary restarts of every instance.

exercises.prompt: A shared database is down for two minutes. What happens if every instance includes database health in liveness?
options: Instances repeatedly restart even though restarting does not repair the database.
The database automatically recovers.
Nothing happens.
Only one instance restarts.
exercises.explanation: Liveness should assess whether the process itself can recover. Shared-dependency failures need a separate readiness or application error strategy.

exercises.prompt: Add readiness at /actuator/health/readiness and liveness at /actuator/health/liveness, both on port 8080.
exercises.explanation: Boot enables Kubernetes probe health groups when Kubernetes is detected; enable probes explicitly for local experiments.
